project: Ordivanta - Manufacturing Workforce Scheduling & Task Allocation System

module_1.name: Workforce Shift Planning and Optimization
module_1.focus: Macro-level shift scheduling: constructing feasible workforce rosters over multi-day horizons while balancing demand coverage, labor utilization, cost, overtime, and workload fairness.

module_2.name: Skill-Based Personnel Task Allocation
module_2.focus: Micro-level workstation task scheduling: allocating qualified workers to non-overlapping fixed-time operations while respecting skills, temporal conflicts, and minimizing active shifts / workers.

datasets.module_alignment: Module 1: Workforce Shift Planning and Optimization
datasets.citation: Côté, M. C., Gendreau, M., & Rousseau, L. M. (2011). Grammar-based integer programming models for multi-activity shift scheduling. INFORMS Journal on Computing, 25(3), 391-408.

instance_summary.file_format: Custom space-delimited text (.txt) and XML roster (.ros)

supported: Demand coverage per 15-minute slot and workstation task
Single task assignment per employee per time slot (sum_j x_{ijt} <= 1)
Worker workstation qualification and skill compatibility
Individual employee maximum scheduled working minutes
unsupported_or_relaxed: Complex multi-window meal break placement within shift span

datasets.license: Academic Research & Benchmark Use (Open Public Benchmark)

datasets.citation: Krishnamoorthy, M., Ernst, A. T., & Baatar, D. (2012). Algorithms for large scale personnel task scheduling. European Journal of Operational Research, 219(3), 677-687.
datasets.domain: Continuous Task Allocation & Multi-Skilled Personnel Assignment

supported: Coverage: Exactly 1 qualified personnel per discrete task
Qualification matching: Strict worker-to-task skill compatibility matrix
Temporal conflict non-overlap: For overlapping tasks i and j, x_{wi} + x_{wj} <= 1
Maximum daily working hours per worker
unsupported_or_relaxed: Physical transit matrix between shop-floor workstations

datasets.official_name: Shift Minimisation Personnel Task Scheduling Problem (SMPTSP)
datasets.module_alignment: Module 2: Skill-Based Personnel Task Allocation (Secondary / Shift Minimization)
datasets.citation: Smet, P., Wauters, T., Mihaylov, M., & Vanden Berghe, G. (2014). The shift minimisation personnel task scheduling problem: a new mathematical model and computational study. Computers & Operations Research, 45, 11-20.
datasets.domain: Personnel Task Allocation with Shift Count Minimization

supported: Coverage: Every task assigned to exactly 1 qualified worker
Worker eligibility: Strict multi-skilling profile matching
Temporal non-overlap: Pairwise disjoint task execution per worker
Shift Minimisation: Explicit objective to minimize the count of active shifts / utilized workers

supported: Shift demand headcount per day and shift type
Single shift per employee per day
Maximum weekly scheduled hours
unsupported_or_relaxed: Individual day-on / day-off soft preference weights
